title: The world’s third-oldest underground, still one small circle
description: Transport filmmaker Geoff Marshall rides the Glasgow Subway, opened in 1896 after London’s and Budapest’s: one 15-station loop under both banks of the Clyde, with trains small enough to earn the nickname the Clockwork Orange.

title: Building the QE2 in the last great Clyde yard
episode: 1967: Clyde Shipworkers Building the QE2 | Queen of the Clyde | World of Work | BBC Archive
description: BBC footage from 1967 of the workers at John Brown & Company in Clydebank, just downriver from Glasgow, building the liner Queen Elizabeth 2. The yard’s giant 1907 Titan crane still stands on the riverbank.

title: A museum of ordinary Glaswegian life
episode: The History of the People's Palace | Glasgow Histories with Peter Mortimer
description: In Glasgow Museums’ Glasgow Histories series, Peter Mortimer tells the story of the People’s Palace, the 1898 red sandstone museum of the city’s social history on Glasgow Green, the oldest park in the city, with a glasshouse Winter Gardens behind.

title: Virginia leaf and the merchants who grew rich on it
episode: How tobacco farming made Glasgow so wealthy | Union - BBC
description: A clip from the BBC series Union on how the 1707 union with England opened colonial trade to Glasgow, whose tobacco lords grew rich on leaf grown by enslaved people in Virginia. The 1775 Tobacco Merchant’s House survives on Miller Street.

title: Repairing a medieval cathedral the medieval way
episode: Conserving an Icon: Glasgow Cathedral and Medieval Methods of Construction
description: Historic Environment Scotland on conserving Glasgow Cathedral, the 13th-century church on the site of St Mungo’s grave and the only medieval cathedral on the Scottish mainland to come through the 1560 Reformation almost intact.

title: A shipowner’s 9,000 objects in a glass-walled park museum
episode: Inside the new-look Burrell Collection with those who make it tick
description: STV News goes behind the scenes at the Burrell Collection in Pollok Country Park, the art, armour, tapestries and ceramics shipping magnate William Burrell gave the city in 1944, rehoused after a six-year refurbishment that ended in 2022.

title: Trams, locomotives and a tall ship on the riverbank
description: The Daily Record’s short tour of the Riverside Museum, Glasgow’s transport museum, a zigzag shed by architect Zaha Hadid at the mouth of the River Kelvin. The museum keeps old trams, Clyde-built locomotives and the tall ship Glenlee.

title: A tenement flat left as it was in 1965
description: Rick Steves visits the Tenement House in Garnethill, where shorthand typist Agnes Toward lived from 1911 to 1965. The National Trust for Scotland keeps her flat as she left it, with gaslight, a coal range and beds built into wall recesses.

title: Miss Cranston’s tea rooms, restored
place: Mackintosh at the Willow, Sauchiehall Street
description: A Doors Open Days film on the Willow Tea Rooms on Sauchiehall Street, designed by Charles Rennie Mackintosh for tea-room owner Kate Cranston and opened in 1903. A trust rescued the building and reopened it in 2018 as Mackintosh at the Willow.

title: A hill of Victorian merchants’ monuments
episode: Glasgow Necropolis -  Glasgow Doors Open Days Digital Festival 2020
description: The volunteer Friends of Glasgow Necropolis show the garden cemetery opened in 1833 on the hill behind the cathedral, where the city’s merchants and industrialists competed in stone under a column topped by reformer John Knox.

title: A century of the Barras
description: Glasgow Building Preservation Trust marks a hundred years of the Barras, the East End weekend market that Maggie McIver started by renting out barrows, the handcarts that gave it its name, before building the covered market and the Barrowland dance hall.

title: Why the Duke wears a traffic cone
episode: The Duke of Wellington statue; Astonishing Glasgow. Ep19
place: Duke of Wellington statue, Royal Exchange Square
description: The local history channel Astonishing Glasgow on Carlo Marochetti’s 1844 equestrian statue of the Duke of Wellington outside the Gallery of Modern Art, which has worn a traffic cone on its head, put there by late-night climbers, since the 1980s.

title: The rent strike that beat Glasgow’s landlords
episode: Mary Barbour's Army - The Woman Who Stood Up For Glasgow's Workers
description: Scottish History Out Of Order on Mary Barbour, the Govan housewife who in 1915 led tenants against wartime rent rises; the strike forced Parliament to freeze rents. Her statue, leading a crowd of women, stands at Govan Cross.

title: The only house left from medieval Glasgow
episode: Exploring the history of Glasgow's historic Provan's Lordship #history #news #glasgow #archive
description: STV News on Provan’s Lordship, built in 1471 opposite the cathedral as part of a hospital, the oldest house in Glasgow and one of just four medieval buildings left in the city. It is now a free museum with a physic garden behind it.

title: Religion, Ireland and ninety minutes of football
description: The Department of Information on the Old Firm, the rivalry between Glasgow’s Celtic and Rangers, rooted in Irish Catholic immigration and Protestant loyalism. Celtic play at Celtic Park in the East End, known locally as Parkhead.
